01-01.title: The World Trade Organization is born
01-01.body: The WTO came into being, replacing the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade of 1947. It gave the world a permanent body to set and police the rules of international trade and to settle disputes between member states.

01-02.title: Stardust probe samples a comet
01-02.body: NASA's Stardust probe flew through the coma of comet Wild 2 and captured dust particles in aerogel. The samples, returned to Earth in 2006, were the first material collected from a comet and revealed minerals formed at high temperature near the young Sun.

01-03.title: The first bitcoin block is mined
01-03.body: Satoshi Nakamoto mined the genesis block of the bitcoin network, launching the first decentralised cryptocurrency. Its underlying blockchain technology went on to inspire thousands of digital currencies and a wide debate about money without central banks.

01-04.title: Burj Khalifa opens in Dubai
01-04.body: The Burj Khalifa officially opened in Dubai. At 828 metres it became the tallest structure ever built, a symbol of the Gulf's rapid growth and a showcase of new engineering for supertall buildings.

01-05.title: Taiwan's high-speed railway opens
01-05.body: Taiwan High Speed Rail began service between Taipei and Kaohsiung, cutting the journey along the island's west coast to about 90 minutes. Built with Japanese Shinkansen technology, it reshaped travel and regional development in Taiwan.

01-06.title: First Asian Socialist Conference opens
01-06.body: Socialist parties from across Asia met in Rangoon, Burma, for the inaugural Asian Socialist Conference. Newly independent nations used it to chart a democratic socialist path distinct from both Western capitalism and Soviet communism.

01-07.title: Galileo first sees Jupiter's moons
01-07.body: Looking through his improved telescope, Galileo Galilei observed what turned out to be the four largest moons of Jupiter. Bodies orbiting another planet were powerful evidence against the idea that everything circles the Earth.

01-08.title: Wilson announces the Fourteen Points
01-08.body: US President Woodrow Wilson set out his Fourteen Points, a programme for peace after the First World War. Its call for open diplomacy, self-determination and a league of nations shaped the peace talks and the League of Nations.

01-09.title: First planets beyond the Solar System confirmed
01-09.body: Radio astronomers Aleksander Wolszczan and Dale Frail announced two planets orbiting the pulsar PSR B1257+12. They were the first confirmed exoplanets, opening a field that has since catalogued thousands of worlds around other stars.

01-10.title: Fritz Lang's Metropolis premieres
01-10.body: Fritz Lang's silent film Metropolis was released in Germany. Its vision of a futuristic city divided between rulers and workers became one of the most influential works of science fiction cinema.

01-11.title: Herschel discovers two moons of Uranus
01-11.body: William Herschel, who had found Uranus six years earlier, discovered its two largest moons, later named Titania and Oberon. They were the first moons found around a planet unknown to the ancients.

01-12.title: The Zanzibar Revolution
01-12.body: Rebels led by John Okello overthrew the Sultan of Zanzibar, ending some two centuries of Arab-dominated rule on the islands. Within months Zanzibar united with Tanganyika to form Tanzania.

01-13.title: Mexico's first feminist congress meets
01-13.body: The First Feminist Congress of Yucatán opened in Mérida, Mexico, during the Mexican Revolution. Delegates debated women's education, legal rights and suffrage, making it a landmark of early feminism in Latin America.

01-14.title: Dutch capture Malacca from Portugal
01-14.body: After a siege of more than five months, Dutch forces and their Johor allies took the fortress of Malacca from the Portuguese. Control of the strait shifted to the Dutch East India Company, ending Portugal's dominance of the region's trade.

01-15.title: Alvor Agreement on Angolan independence
01-15.body: Portugal and Angola's three nationalist movements, the MPLA, FNLA and UNITA, signed the Alvor Agreement, setting independence for November 1975. The fragile power-sharing deal soon collapsed into a long civil war.

01-16.title: Octavian receives the title Augustus
01-16.body: The Roman Senate granted Octavian the name Augustus. The honour marked his position as the first Roman emperor and the transition from the Roman Republic to the Roman Empire.

01-17.title: Cook crosses the Antarctic Circle
01-17.body: On James Cook's second voyage, HMS Resolution became the first ship known to cross the Antarctic Circle. The voyage showed that any southern continent lay far south, in the ice, ending hopes of a rich temperate landmass.

01-18.title: The First Fleet reaches Botany Bay
01-18.body: HMS Supply, the first ship of the First Fleet, arrived at Botany Bay carrying convicts and marines from Britain. The fleet soon moved to Port Jackson, founding the colony that became Sydney and beginning British settlement of Australia.

01-19.title: The Batavian Republic is proclaimed
01-19.body: A day after Stadtholder William V fled, revolutionaries in Amsterdam proclaimed the Batavian Republic, ending the old Dutch Republic. The new state, allied with revolutionary France, introduced reforms that shaped the modern Netherlands.

01-20.title: De Montfort's Parliament meets
01-20.body: Simon de Montfort convened a parliament in London that included elected representatives of towns as well as knights of the shires. It is seen as a forerunner of the English House of Commons.

01-21.title: Ireland's First Dáil declares independence
01-21.body: The First Dáil met at the Mansion House in Dublin and adopted a declaration of independence for an Irish Republic. The same day saw the first shots of the Irish War of Independence.

01-22.title: The jumbo jet enters service
01-22.body: The Boeing 747, the first wide-body airliner, flew its first commercial service with Pan Am between New York and London. Its huge capacity cut the cost of long-haul flights and helped make air travel a mass experience.

01-23.title: The Hongwu Emperor founds the Ming dynasty
01-23.body: Zhu Yuanzhang, a former peasant and monk, ascended the throne as the Hongwu Emperor, founding the Ming dynasty. The Ming ruled China for nearly three centuries after driving out the Mongol Yuan.

01-24.title: University of Calcutta is founded
01-24.body: The University of Calcutta was established, the first university in South Asia on the modern Western model. It produced generations of scholars, reformers and leaders of the Indian independence movement.

01-25.title: Egypt's revolution begins in Tahrir Square
01-25.body: Protests on a "Day of Anger" launched the Egyptian revolution, part of the Arab Spring. Within 18 days the mass demonstrations forced President Hosni Mubarak from power after nearly 30 years.

01-26.title: India becomes a republic
01-26.body: The Constitution of India came into force, making the country a sovereign republic with Rajendra Prasad as its first president. The date is celebrated every year as Republic Day.

01-27.title: The Canadian Caper rescues six diplomats
01-27.body: Six American diplomats who had escaped the seizure of the US embassy in Tehran left Iran on Canadian passports, posing as a film crew. The covert rescue by Canada and the CIA was later dramatised in the film Argo.

01-28.title: Horace Walpole coins 'serendipity'
01-28.body: In a letter to a friend, Horace Walpole coined the word serendipity, inspired by the Persian tale The Three Princes of Serendip. It names the happy accident of finding something valuable while looking for something else.

01-29.title: Queen Victoria creates the Victoria Cross
01-29.body: Queen Victoria instituted the Victoria Cross to honour acts of valour during the Crimean War. Open to all ranks, it remains the highest award for gallantry in the British and several Commonwealth armed forces.

01-30.title: South Korea's first orbital rocket launch
01-30.body: South Korea launched the Naro-1 rocket from the Naro Space Center, placing a satellite in orbit at the third attempt. It made South Korea one of the few nations to reach orbit from its own territory.

01-31.title: Final Fantasy VII is released
01-31.body: Square released Final Fantasy VII in Japan, the first game in the series with 3D graphics. Its cinematic storytelling made it a global bestseller and popularised Japanese role-playing games worldwide.

02-01.title: Koxinga ends Dutch rule in Taiwan
02-01.body: After a nine-month siege of Fort Zeelandia, the Ming loyalist Zheng Chenggong (Koxinga) secured the surrender of the Dutch East India Company. It ended Dutch colonial rule in Taiwan and established the Kingdom of Tungning on the island.

02-02.title: Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo ends a war
02-02.body: The treaty ending the Mexican–American War was signed. Mexico ceded about half its territory, including California and much of the American Southwest, to the United States in return for 15 million dollars.

02-03.title: San Martín wins at San Lorenzo
02-03.body: José de San Martín and his newly formed Mounted Grenadiers defeated Spanish royalist forces at San Lorenzo on the Paraná River. It was his first battle in South America and the start of a campaign that helped free Argentina, Chile and Peru.

02-04.title: Tischendorf finds the Codex Sinaiticus
02-04.body: At Saint Catherine's Monastery in Sinai, Constantin von Tischendorf found the Codex Sinaiticus, a 4th-century manuscript of the Bible in Greek. It contains the oldest complete New Testament and transformed biblical scholarship.

02-05.title: The Welcome Stranger gold nugget found
02-05.body: Two prospectors at Moliagul in Victoria, Australia, unearthed the Welcome Stranger, just below the surface. It remains the largest alluvial gold nugget ever found, a symbol of the Victorian gold rush.

02-06.title: Raffles founds modern Singapore
02-06.body: Stamford Raffles signed a treaty with the Sultan of Johor allowing the British East India Company to set up a trading post on Singapore. Its free port grew into one of the world's great trading cities.

02-07.title: Maastricht Treaty creates the European Union
02-07.body: Members of the European Communities signed the Maastricht Treaty, creating the European Union. It laid the path to a single currency, the euro, and to common foreign and justice policies.

02-08.title: Boy Scouts of America founded
02-08.body: Publisher William D. Boyce incorporated the Boy Scouts of America, bringing Robert Baden-Powell's Scout movement to the United States. It became one of the country's largest youth organisations.

02-09.title: Svalbard Treaty signed in Paris
02-09.body: The Svalbard Treaty recognised Norwegian sovereignty over the Arctic archipelago while giving all signatory nations equal rights to its resources. It also made Svalbard a demilitarised zone, an unusual model of shared access.

02-10.title: Deep Blue beats Kasparov in a game
02-10.body: IBM's Deep Blue became the first computer to beat a reigning world chess champion in a game under tournament conditions, defeating Garry Kasparov in Philadelphia. Kasparov won the match, but lost the 1997 rematch.

02-11.title: Nelson Mandela walks free
02-11.body: After 27 years as a political prisoner, Nelson Mandela was released from Victor Verster Prison near Paarl. His release opened negotiations to end apartheid, and in 1994 he became South Africa's first democratically elected president.

02-12.title: NEAR Shoemaker lands on an asteroid
02-12.body: NASA's NEAR Shoemaker probe touched down on the asteroid 433 Eros after a year in orbit. It was the first spacecraft ever to land on an asteroid, though it had not been designed to do so.

02-13.title: The Nashville sit-ins begin
02-13.body: African-American college students sat at segregated lunch counters in Nashville, Tennessee, refusing to leave. Their disciplined nonviolent campaign desegregated the city's lunch counters and became a model for the civil rights movement.

02-14.title: The Importance of Being Earnest premieres
02-14.body: Oscar Wilde's comedy The Importance of Being Earnest opened at the St James's Theatre in London. Its witty satire of Victorian manners has made it one of the most performed and quoted plays in English.

02-15.title: Millions march against the Iraq War
02-15.body: Millions of people in some 600 to 800 cities around the world protested against the planned invasion of Iraq. It is often described as the largest coordinated protest in history.

02-16.title: Southern Cross Expedition reaches the Ice Barrier
02-16.body: Carsten Borchgrevink's Southern Cross Expedition made the first landing on the Great Ice Barrier and set a new Farthest South record. The expedition, the first to winter on the Antarctic mainland, opened the heroic age of Antarctic exploration.

02-17.title: France captures the Citadel of Saigon
02-17.body: French naval forces captured the Citadel of Saigon from the Nguyễn dynasty. The campaign began French colonial rule in southern Vietnam, which expanded into French Indochina.

02-18.title: Space Shuttle Enterprise first takes flight
02-18.body: NASA's prototype orbiter Enterprise flew for the first time, carried on top of a modified Boeing 747. The approach and landing tests that followed proved that the Space Shuttle could glide and land like an aircraft.

02-19.title: The Feminine Mystique is published
02-19.body: Betty Friedan's The Feminine Mystique challenged the idea that women found fulfilment only as housewives. The bestseller is widely credited with sparking second-wave feminism in the United States.

02-20.title: A volcano is born in a Mexican cornfield
02-20.body: A fissure opened in a farmer's cornfield in Michoacán, Mexico, and grew into the Parícutin volcano. It erupted for nine years, giving scientists the first chance to document a volcano's whole life from its birth.

02-21.title: The Cherokee Phoenix is first published
02-21.body: The Cherokee Phoenix, the first newspaper published by Native Americans and the first in a Native American language, appeared in New Echota, Georgia. It used the syllabary created by Sequoyah and printed in both Cherokee and English.

02-22.title: Dolly the cloned sheep is announced
02-22.body: Scientists at the Roslin Institute in Scotland announced Dolly, the first mammal cloned from an adult cell. Her birth proved that specialised adult cells could be reprogrammed, transforming research on stem cells.

02-23.title: Supernova 1987A lights up the southern sky
02-23.body: Light from a supernova in the Large Magellanic Cloud reached Earth, the nearest observed since 1604. SN 1987A was the first supernova studied with modern instruments, and the first detected through neutrinos.

02-24.title: Treaty of Yandabo ends Anglo-Burmese War
02-24.body: The Treaty of Yandabo ended the First Anglo-Burmese War. Burma ceded Assam, Manipur, Arakan and Tenasserim to the British East India Company, the first step in the British conquest of Burma.

02-25.title: People Power ends Marcos rule
02-25.body: After days of peaceful mass protests in Manila, Ferdinand Marcos fled the Philippines and Corazon Aquino became president. The People Power Revolution inspired nonviolent movements for democracy around the world.

02-26.title: First recorded European landing in Australia
02-26.body: Dutch navigator Willem Janszoon and the crew of the Duyfken landed on the western shore of Cape York Peninsula. It was the first recorded European landing in Australia, though Janszoon believed he was on New Guinea.

02-27.title: Japan adopts the rising sun flag
02-27.body: Japan's government adopted the Hinomaru, a red disc on a white field, as the civil ensign for merchant ships. The simple design later became the national flag of Japan.

02-28.title: First gamma-ray burst afterglow detected
02-28.body: Satellites detected GRB 970228, an 80-second burst of gamma rays. It was the first burst whose afterglow was observed, providing evidence that gamma-ray bursts occur in distant galaxies.

02-29.title: Tokyo Skytree is completed
02-29.body: Construction of Tokyo Skytree finished. At 634 metres, the broadcasting tower is the tallest tower in the world and the tallest structure in Japan.

03-01.title: Ethiopia defeats Italy at Adwa
03-01.body: Emperor Menelik II's army decisively defeated an Italian invasion force at Adwa, ending the First Italo-Ethiopian War. Ethiopia kept its independence, and the victory became a lasting symbol of African resistance to colonialism.

03-02.title: Concorde makes its first flight
03-02.body: The Anglo-French Concorde prototype took off for the first time from Toulouse. Entering service in 1976, it carried passengers across the Atlantic at twice the speed of sound for 27 years.

03-03.title: Bizet's Carmen premieres in Paris
03-03.body: Georges Bizet's opera Carmen opened at the Opéra-Comique in Paris to a cool reception. Its fiery heroine and tunes such as the Habanera made it one of the most performed operas in the world.

03-04.title: PlayStation 2 goes on sale
03-04.body: Sony released the PlayStation 2 in Japan. With a built-in DVD player and a large library of games, it became the best-selling video game console of all time.

03-05.title: Korda photographs Che Guevara
03-05.body: At a memorial service in Havana, Cuban photographer Alberto Korda captured Che Guevara in the portrait known as Guerrillero Heroico. It became one of the most reproduced images in history and a global icon of rebellion.

03-06.title: Verdi's La traviata premieres
03-06.body: Giuseppe Verdi's La traviata opened at La Fenice in Venice. Its first night was a failure, but after revisions the tragic story of the courtesan Violetta became one of the best-loved operas.

03-07.title: Bloody Sunday at Selma
03-07.body: State troopers attacked civil rights marchers on the Edmund Pettus Bridge in Selma, Alabama. Televised images of the violence built national support for the Voting Rights Act, signed that August.

03-08.title: Nader Shah is crowned in Iran
03-08.body: Nader, a military commander of humble origins, was crowned Shah of Iran, founding the Afsharid dynasty. He went on to build a vast empire, invading India and sacking Delhi in 1739.

03-09.title: Adam Smith publishes The Wealth of Nations
03-09.body: Scottish philosopher Adam Smith published An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations. Its analysis of markets, specialisation and free trade founded modern economics.

03-10.title: The Tibetan uprising begins
03-10.body: Thousands of Tibetans surrounded the Potala Palace in Lhasa to protect the Dalai Lama from Chinese authorities. The uprising was crushed, and the Dalai Lama fled into exile in India, where he has led Tibetans abroad ever since.

03-11.title: The Flagstaff War begins in New Zealand
03-11.body: Māori forces led by Hōne Heke and Te Ruki Kawiti attacked the British settlement of Kororāreka, after Heke had repeatedly cut down the flagstaff there. The conflict was the first of the New Zealand Wars.

03-12.title: Gandhi begins the Salt March
03-12.body: Mahatma Gandhi set out from his ashram with 78 followers on a 24-day walk to the sea at Dandi to make salt in defiance of the British salt tax. The march drew mass support and made civil disobedience a central weapon of India's independence struggle.

03-13.title: The Seikan Tunnel opens
03-13.body: The Seikan Tunnel opened, linking Honshu and Hokkaido by rail beneath the Tsugaru Strait. At almost 54 km, it was the world's longest railway tunnel for nearly three decades.

03-14.title: India's first talking film premieres
03-14.body: Alam Ara, the first Indian sound film, opened at the Majestic Cinema in Bombay. Its songs set the pattern of music-filled films that defines Indian cinema to this day.

03-15.title: Julius Caesar is assassinated
03-15.body: On the Ides of March, Julius Caesar was killed by a group of Roman senators led by Brutus and Cassius, who feared his power. The plot failed to save the Republic: the civil wars that followed led to rule by emperors.

03-16.title: Nebuchadnezzar captures Jerusalem
03-16.body: The Babylonian king Nebuchadnezzar II took Jerusalem and replaced King Jehoiachin with Zedekiah. Many of Judah's elite were deported to Babylon, beginning the Babylonian captivity central to Jewish history.

03-17.title: Californium is announced
03-17.body: Scientists at the University of California, Berkeley announced that they had created element 98, californium. It was the sixth transuranium element made, and is used today as a powerful neutron source.

03-18.title: Alexei Leonov makes the first spacewalk
03-18.body: Soviet cosmonaut Alexei Leonov left Voskhod 2 and floated in space for about 12 minutes, the first person to do so. His suit swelled in the vacuum and he had to let out air to get back inside.

03-19.title: Brazil's March of the Family
03-19.body: Hundreds of thousands marched in São Paulo against President João Goulart and communism. The march showed middle-class support for the military coup that toppled Goulart less than two weeks later, beginning 21 years of military rule.

03-20.title: The Dutch East India Company is founded
03-20.body: The States General of the Netherlands chartered the Dutch East India Company with a monopoly on Asian trade. Often called the first multinational corporation, it was also the first company to issue shares to the public.

03-21.title: The Sharpeville massacre
03-21.body: South African police opened fire on a crowd protesting against pass laws at Sharpeville, killing 69 people. The massacre turned world opinion against apartheid, and the day is now Human Rights Day in South Africa.

03-22.title: Comet Hale–Bopp makes its closest approach
03-22.body: Comet Hale–Bopp passed closest to Earth. Visible to the naked eye for a record 18 months, it was one of the most widely observed comets of the 20th century.

03-23.title: The Ahmadiyya movement is founded
03-23.body: Mirza Ghulam Ahmad accepted the first pledges of allegiance from his followers in Ludhiana, British India, founding the Ahmadiyya movement in Islam. The community now has millions of members in more than 200 countries.

03-24.title: Robert Koch identifies the tuberculosis germ
03-24.body: German physician Robert Koch announced that he had identified the bacterium that causes tuberculosis. The discovery transformed the fight against the disease, and the date is marked as World Tuberculosis Day.

03-25.title: Britain abolishes the slave trade
03-25.body: The Slave Trade Act received royal assent, making the Atlantic slave trade illegal throughout the British Empire. It was a milestone for the abolitionist movement, though slavery itself continued in British colonies until 1834.

03-26.title: Women hug trees in the Chipko movement
03-26.body: In the Himalayan village of Reni, women led by Gaura Devi stood guard around trees to stop loggers from felling them. The protest became the emblem of the Chipko movement, an early landmark of grassroots environmentalism.

03-27.title: Work starts on the Trans-Alaska Pipeline
03-27.body: Construction began on the Trans-Alaska Pipeline, built to carry oil 1,287 km from Prudhoe Bay to the port of Valdez. It was one of the largest private construction projects of its time.

03-28.title: Olbers discovers the asteroid Pallas
03-28.body: German astronomer Heinrich Olbers discovered Pallas, the second asteroid ever found. Considered a planet at first, it helped astronomers realise there was a whole belt of small bodies between Mars and Jupiter.

03-29.title: Farmers discover the Terracotta Army
03-29.body: Farmers digging a well in Shaanxi, China, found fragments of the Terracotta Army. The thousands of life-size clay soldiers buried with the first emperor, Qin Shi Huang, are among the greatest archaeological discoveries ever made.

03-30.title: Morocco becomes a French protectorate
03-30.body: Sultan Abd al-Hafid signed the Treaty of Fes, placing most of Morocco under French protection. The country did not regain full independence until 1956.

03-31.title: Japan opens its ports to America
03-31.body: Commodore Matthew Perry and the Tokugawa shogunate signed the Convention of Kanagawa, opening two Japanese ports to American ships. It ended more than two centuries of Japanese isolation and set Japan on the road to modernisation.

04-01.title: Apple Computer is founded
04-01.body: Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak and Ronald Wayne founded Apple Computer to sell Wozniak's Apple I. The company went on to popularise the personal computer, the smartphone and the tablet, becoming one of the most valuable firms in the world.

04-02.title: 2001: A Space Odyssey premieres
04-02.body: Stanley Kubrick's 2001: A Space Odyssey premiered in Washington, D.C. Its realistic depiction of spaceflight and its enigmatic story set a new standard for science fiction cinema, a year before the first Moon landing.

04-03.title: Rakesh Sharma becomes India's first spaceman
04-03.body: Indian Air Force pilot Rakesh Sharma launched aboard Soyuz T-11 to the Soviet Salyut 7 space station. He spent nearly eight days in orbit and remains a national hero in India.

04-04.title: The North Atlantic Treaty creates NATO
04-04.body: Twelve nations signed the North Atlantic Treaty in Washington, D.C., founding NATO. Its promise that an attack on one member is an attack on all became the cornerstone of Western security during the Cold War.

04-05.title: Akashi Kaikyo Bridge opens in Japan
04-05.body: The Akashi Kaikyo Bridge, linking Kobe with Awaji Island, opened to traffic. Its central span of nearly two kilometres made it the world's longest suspension bridge for 24 years.

04-06.title: Van Riebeeck founds the Cape settlement
04-06.body: Jan van Riebeeck of the Dutch East India Company landed at Table Bay to set up a supply station for ships sailing to Asia. The outpost grew into Cape Town and marked the beginning of European settlement in South Africa.

04-07.title: The World Health Organization is founded
04-07.body: The WHO's constitution came into force, creating a United Nations agency for international public health. It went on to lead the eradication of smallpox, and the date is celebrated as World Health Day.

04-08.title: The Venus de Milo is discovered
04-08.body: A farmer on the Greek island of Milos uncovered an ancient marble statue of a woman, now known as the Venus de Milo. Acquired by France, it became one of the most famous works in the Louvre.

04-09.title: The oldest known recording of a human voice
04-09.body: Édouard-Léon Scott de Martinville recorded someone singing "Au clair de la lune" on his phonautograph, which traced sound waves on paper. The recording, made to be seen rather than heard, was first played back in 2008.

04-10.title: Mount Tambora's great eruption begins
04-10.body: Mount Tambora on the Indonesian island of Sumbawa began the most powerful volcanic eruption in recorded history. Its ash cooled the planet, leading to 1816's "Year Without a Summer" and crop failures across the Northern Hemisphere.

04-11.title: The Emirate of Transjordan is founded
04-11.body: Emir Abdullah set up the first central government of Transjordan, a British-protected emirate. It became fully independent in 1946 and is today the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan.

04-12.title: Yuri Gagarin becomes the first human in space
04-12.body: Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin orbited the Earth once aboard Vostok 1 in a flight of 108 minutes. His triumph opened the era of human spaceflight and spurred the United States to aim for the Moon.

04-13.title: Handel's Messiah premieres in Dublin
04-13.body: George Frideric Handel's oratorio Messiah was first performed at a charity concert in Dublin. With its famous Hallelujah chorus, it became one of the most frequently performed choral works in Western music.

04-14.title: The Second Spanish Republic is proclaimed
04-14.body: After republicans won municipal elections, King Alfonso XIII left Spain and the Second Spanish Republic was proclaimed. Its reforms divided the country, and it fell at the end of the Spanish Civil War in 1939.

04-15.title: Jackie Robinson breaks baseball's colour line
04-15.body: Jackie Robinson played first base for the Brooklyn Dodgers, the first African American in Major League Baseball in the modern era. His courage under abuse made him a pioneer of the civil rights movement.

04-16.title: The Battle of Mount Tabor
04-16.body: During Napoleon's campaign in Egypt and Syria, a small French force under Kléber held off a much larger Ottoman army near Mount Tabor until Napoleon arrived to rout it. Napoleon's Syrian campaign failed weeks later at Acre.

04-17.title: Britain's first national park
04-17.body: The Peak District in the English Midlands became the first national park in the United Kingdom. It followed decades of campaigning for public access to the countryside, including the 1932 mass trespass of Kinder Scout.

04-18.title: Zimbabwe becomes independent
04-18.body: Zimbabwe gained internationally recognised independence from Britain after years of guerrilla war against the white-minority government of Rhodesia. Robert Mugabe became the first prime minister.

04-19.title: India launches its first satellite
04-19.body: Aryabhata, India's first satellite, was launched by a Soviet rocket from Kapustin Yar. Named after the 5th-century mathematician, it marked the start of India's space programme.

04-20.title: Caillié reaches Timbuktu
04-20.body: French explorer René Caillié arrived in Timbuktu, travelling in disguise. He became the first European to visit the legendary city in Mali and return alive to describe it.

04-21.title: Brasília is inaugurated as Brazil's capital
04-21.body: Brasília, a new city built in the interior in just 41 months, replaced Rio de Janeiro as the capital of Brazil. Planned by Lúcio Costa with buildings by Oscar Niemeyer, it is a landmark of modernist architecture.

04-22.title: Persians and English take Hormuz
04-22.body: After a siege by Safavid Persian troops supported by English ships, the Portuguese fortress on Hormuz Island surrendered. It ended more than a century of Portuguese control over the entrance to the Persian Gulf.

04-23.title: Turkey's Grand National Assembly first meets
04-23.body: During the Turkish War of Independence, the Grand National Assembly convened in Ankara under Mustafa Kemal. It led the resistance and in 1923 proclaimed the Republic of Turkey; the date is now a national holiday.

04-24.title: The Hubble Space Telescope is launched
04-24.body: The Space Shuttle Discovery carried the Hubble Space Telescope into orbit. After a flaw in its mirror was corrected in 1993, Hubble produced images that transformed astronomy, from the age of the universe to distant galaxies.

04-25.title: Anzac troops land at Gallipoli
04-25.body: Australian and New Zealand troops landed at what became Anzac Cove, beginning the Allied campaign on the Gallipoli peninsula. The campaign failed, but the date is commemorated as Anzac Day in both countries.

04-26.title: Tanganyika and Zanzibar unite
04-26.body: The republics of Tanganyika and Zanzibar merged, with Julius Nyerere as president. Later that year the union took the name Tanzania.

04-27.title: Sierra Leone gains independence
04-27.body: Sierra Leone became independent from Britain, with Milton Margai as its first prime minister. Founded as a home for freed slaves, its capital Freetown had long been a centre of education in West Africa.

04-28.title: The Mutiny on the Bounty
04-28.body: In the South Pacific, Fletcher Christian led a mutiny aboard HMS Bounty and set Captain William Bligh adrift in a small boat. Bligh navigated 6,700 km to Timor, while the mutineers settled on Pitcairn Island.

04-29.title: Chemical Weapons Convention comes into force
04-29.body: The Chemical Weapons Convention entered into force, banning the development, production, stockpiling and use of chemical weapons. Its watchdog, the OPCW, has overseen the destruction of most declared stockpiles.

04-30.title: The Louisiana Purchase
04-30.body: The United States agreed to buy France's vast Louisiana territory for 15 million dollars. The deal roughly doubled the size of the young country and opened the way to westward expansion.

05-01.title: Vivekananda founds the Ramakrishna Mission
05-01.body: Swami Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission in Calcutta, combining Hindu spiritual teaching with social service. It runs schools, hospitals and relief work across India and beyond.

05-02.title: Ethiopia and Italy sign the Treaty of Wuchale
05-02.body: Emperor Menelik II and Italy signed the Treaty of Wuchale. The Italian text claimed a protectorate over Ethiopia while the Amharic text did not, and the dispute led to the war that ended at Adwa in 1896.

05-03.title: Japan's postwar constitution takes effect
05-03.body: Japan's new constitution came into force, making the emperor a symbol of the state, guaranteeing fundamental rights and renouncing war. It has never been amended.

05-04.title: The May Fourth Movement begins
05-04.body: Students in Beijing protested against the Paris Peace Conference's decision to hand German rights in Shandong to Japan. The protests grew into a movement for science, democracy and a new vernacular culture that shaped modern China.

05-05.title: Alan Shepard becomes the first American in space
05-05.body: Astronaut Alan Shepard flew a 15-minute suborbital flight in the Freedom 7 capsule, the first American in space. Less than three weeks later, President Kennedy committed the nation to landing on the Moon.

05-06.title: Roger Bannister runs the four-minute mile
05-06.body: At Iffley Road track in Oxford, medical student Roger Bannister ran a mile in 3 minutes 59.4 seconds. Breaking a barrier many thought impossible made him one of the most famous athletes of his time.

05-07.title: Robespierre establishes the Cult of the Supreme Being
05-07.body: During the French Revolution, the National Convention adopted Robespierre's decree establishing the Cult of the Supreme Being as a civic religion. Its grand festival a month later fed fears of his ambitions and he fell in July.

05-08.title: The Tollund Man is discovered
05-08.body: Peat cutters near Silkeborg, Denmark, found the remarkably preserved body of a man who lived around 400 BC. The Tollund Man is one of the best-preserved bog bodies ever found, his face still clearly recognisable.

05-09.title: Battle of Heligoland in the North Sea
05-09.body: A Danish squadron fought an Austrian and Prussian force off Heligoland during the Second Schleswig War. It was one of the last battles between squadrons of wooden warships, and the last major naval battle fought by Denmark.

05-10.title: Han astronomers record a sunspot
05-10.body: Astronomers of China's Han dynasty recorded a dark spot on the Sun. It is the earliest precisely dated sunspot observation, from a tradition of systematic sky-watching that long outpaced Europe's.

05-11.title: The Diamond Sutra is printed
05-11.body: A copy of the Buddhist Diamond Sutra was printed from wooden blocks in Tang China, with a dated colophon. Found in a cave at Dunhuang, it is the oldest known dated printed book.

05-12.title: Konrad Zuse presents the Z3 computer
05-12.body: German engineer Konrad Zuse demonstrated the Z3 in Berlin. Built from telephone relays, it was the world's first working programmable, fully automatic digital computer.

05-13.title: Zakir Husain becomes India's president
05-13.body: Educationist Zakir Husain took office as the third President of India, the first Muslim to hold the post. A founder of Jamia Millia Islamia, he embodied India's secular ideals.

05-14.title: Lewis and Clark set out west
05-14.body: The Corps of Discovery under Meriwether Lewis and William Clark left Camp Dubois near St. Louis. Their journey to the Pacific and back mapped the newly purchased Louisiana Territory and beyond.

05-15.title: Okinawa returns to Japan
05-15.body: The United States returned Okinawa and the other Ryukyu Islands to Japan, ending 27 years of American administration after the Second World War. Large US military bases remain on Okinawa.

05-16.title: The first laser shines
05-16.body: Physicist Theodore Maiman operated the first working laser at Hughes Research Laboratories in California, using a ruby crystal. Lasers now underpin technologies from fibre-optic communications to surgery.

05-17.title: Brown v. Board of Education decided
05-17.body: The US Supreme Court ruled unanimously that racial segregation in public schools was unconstitutional, declaring separate facilities "inherently unequal". The decision was a turning point for the civil rights movement.

05-18.title: India tests its first nuclear device
05-18.body: India carried out an underground nuclear test, code-named Smiling Buddha, at Pokhran in Rajasthan. It was the first confirmed nuclear test by a country outside the five permanent members of the UN Security Council.

05-19.title: Franklin sails for the Northwest Passage
05-19.body: Sir John Franklin left England with HMS Erebus and HMS Terror to find the Northwest Passage through the Arctic. The ships became trapped in ice and all 129 men were lost; searches for them mapped much of the Canadian Arctic.

05-20.title: The Metre Convention is signed
05-20.body: Seventeen nations signed the Metre Convention in Paris, creating the International Bureau of Weights and Measures. It laid the foundation of the International System of Units used worldwide today; 20 May is World Metrology Day.

05-21.title: Lindbergh lands in Paris
05-21.body: Charles Lindbergh landed at Le Bourget after flying the Spirit of St. Louis alone and non-stop from New York in 33.5 hours. The flight made him a global celebrity and boosted public faith in aviation.

05-22.title: Ceylon becomes the Republic of Sri Lanka
05-22.body: A new constitution came into force, replacing the Dominion of Ceylon with the Republic of Sri Lanka. The country cut its last constitutional ties to the British Crown while remaining in the Commonwealth.

05-23.title: The North-West Mounted Police is created
05-23.body: Canada's Parliament established the North-West Mounted Police to bring law and order to its vast western territories. The force became the Royal Canadian Mounted Police, the famous Mounties.

05-24.title: Amy Johnson lands in Australia
05-24.body: English aviator Amy Johnson landed in Darwin after flying solo from England in 19 days, the first woman to do so. Her 18,000 km flight made her an international celebrity.

05-25.title: Argentina's May Revolution
05-25.body: A crowd in Buenos Aires backed the creation of the Primera Junta, deposing the Spanish viceroy. It was the first step towards Argentine independence, and 25 May is a national holiday.

05-26.title: The Beatles release Sgt. Pepper
05-26.body: The Beatles released Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band in Britain. Its studio experimentation and conception as a whole album rather than a set of singles made it a landmark of popular music.

05-27.title: Australians vote for Aboriginal inclusion
05-27.body: Over 90 per cent of Australian voters approved changes allowing Aboriginal people to be counted in the census and the federal government to make laws for them. It was the most successful referendum in Australian history.

05-28.title: An eclipse halts the Battle of Halys
05-28.body: According to Herodotus, a solar eclipse predicted by Thales of Miletus stopped a battle between the Lydians and the Medes, who made peace. Astronomers date it to 28 May 585 BC, making it one of the earliest precisely dated events.

05-29.title: Hillary and Tenzing summit Everest
05-29.body: New Zealander Edmund Hillary and Sherpa Tenzing Norgay became the first people confirmed to reach the summit of Mount Everest, the world's highest mountain. The news reached London on the eve of Queen Elizabeth II's coronation.

05-30.title: Auckland Harbour Bridge opens
05-30.body: The Auckland Harbour Bridge opened across Waitematā Harbour, linking central Auckland with the North Shore. It transformed the growth of New Zealand's largest city.

05-31.title: Treaty of Vereeniging ends the Boer War
05-31.body: The Treaty of Vereeniging ended the Second Boer War, and the Boer republics of the Transvaal and Orange Free State came under British rule. They joined the Union of South Africa in 1910.

06-01.title: The Navajo sign the Treaty of Bosque Redondo
06-01.body: The Navajo and the US government signed a treaty ending the Navajo's internment at Bosque Redondo, where thousands had died after the forced Long Walk. It let them return to part of their homeland, the core of today's Navajo Nation.

06-02.title: Coronation of Queen Elizabeth II
06-02.body: Elizabeth II was crowned at Westminster Abbey. It was the first British coronation broadcast on television, watched by millions and helping to popularise TV ownership.

06-03.title: First ascent of an 8,000-metre peak
06-03.body: Maurice Herzog and Louis Lachenal of a French expedition reached the summit of Annapurna in Nepal. It was the first time climbers had stood on any of the world's fourteen peaks above 8,000 metres.

06-04.title: The Battle of Midway begins
06-04.body: Japanese carrier aircraft attacked Midway Atoll in the central Pacific. Forewarned by codebreakers, US forces sank four Japanese carriers in three days, a turning point of the Pacific War.

06-05.title: George Marshall proposes the Marshall Plan
06-05.body: In a speech at Harvard, US Secretary of State George Marshall proposed American aid to rebuild war-torn Europe. The resulting European Recovery Program delivered over 13 billion dollars and spurred European economic cooperation.

06-06.title: Shivaji is crowned Chhatrapati
06-06.body: The Maratha leader Shivaji was crowned at Raigad Fort, taking the title Chhatrapati. His coronation founded the Maratha Empire, which later became the dominant power in India.

06-07.title: Britain's Great Reform Act becomes law
06-07.body: The Reform Act received royal assent, redistributing parliamentary seats from "rotten boroughs" to growing industrial towns and widening the vote. It began the gradual move to democracy in the United Kingdom.

06-08.title: Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four is published
06-08.body: George Orwell's dystopian novel Nineteen Eighty-Four was published in London. Terms such as Big Brother, thoughtcrime and doublethink entered everyday language as warnings about totalitarian control.

06-09.title: First flight across the Pacific
06-09.body: Charles Kingsford Smith and his crew landed the Southern Cross in Brisbane after flying from California via Hawaii and Fiji. It was the first flight across the Pacific Ocean.

06-10.title: The Arab Revolt begins
06-10.body: Sharif Hussein of Mecca launched a revolt against the Ottoman Empire, aiming for an independent Arab state. Supported by Britain, it helped end Ottoman rule in Arabia and the Levant, though the promised unified state never came.

06-11.title: The Stand in the Schoolhouse Door
06-11.body: Governor George Wallace stood at the door of the University of Alabama to block two Black students from enrolling. Faced with federalised National Guard troops, he stepped aside, and the university was desegregated.

06-12.title: Anne Frank begins her diary
06-12.body: On her 13th birthday in Amsterdam, Anne Frank received a diary and began writing in it. Kept while her Jewish family hid from the Nazis, it became one of the most widely read books in the world.

06-13.title: Pioneer 10 passes Neptune's orbit
06-13.body: NASA's Pioneer 10 crossed the orbit of Neptune, then the outermost planet, becoming the first human-made object to leave the region of the major planets. It carries a plaque designed as a message to any finder.

06-14.title: The Stars and Stripes is adopted
06-14.body: The Second Continental Congress resolved that the flag of the United States would have thirteen alternating red and white stripes and thirteen white stars on a blue field. The date is celebrated as Flag Day.

06-15.title: Assyrians record the Bur-Sagale eclipse
06-15.body: Scribes in Assyria recorded a solar eclipse during the year of the official Bur-Sagale. Identified by astronomers as the eclipse of 15 June 763 BC, it anchors the chronology of the ancient Near East.

06-16.title: Valentina Tereshkova becomes the first woman in space
06-16.body: Soviet cosmonaut Valentina Tereshkova launched aboard Vostok 6 and orbited the Earth 48 times in nearly three days. A former textile worker and amateur parachutist, she remains the only woman to have flown solo in space.

06-17.title: Guatemala passes its land reform
06-17.body: Guatemala's Congress passed Decree 900, redistributing uncultivated land on large estates to landless peasants. The reform angered the United Fruit Company and led to the CIA-backed coup of 1954.

06-18.title: Li Yuan founds the Tang dynasty
06-18.body: Li Yuan proclaimed himself emperor, founding the Tang dynasty. The Tang presided over a golden age of Chinese poetry, art and trade, with its capital Chang'an one of the largest cities in the world.

06-19.title: Patent Cooperation Treaty signed
06-19.body: The Patent Cooperation Treaty was signed in Washington, D.C. It lets inventors file a single international application to seek patent protection in many countries, and now covers over 150 states.

06-20.title: The Mali Federation becomes independent
06-20.body: The Mali Federation, uniting Senegal and French Sudan, gained independence from France. It broke apart two months later into the separate states of Senegal and Mali.

06-21.title: The Manchester Baby runs its first program
06-21.body: The Manchester Baby at the University of Manchester ran the first program stored in a computer's electronic memory. It proved the stored-program design used by virtually all computers since.

06-22.title: Germany invades the Soviet Union
06-22.body: Nazi Germany and its allies launched Operation Barbarossa, the largest invasion in history, against the Soviet Union. The war on the Eastern Front became the decisive theatre of the Second World War in Europe.

06-23.title: Nasser is elected President of Egypt
06-23.body: In a referendum, Egyptians approved a new constitution and elected Gamal Abdel Nasser as president. A month later he nationalised the Suez Canal, becoming the leading figure of Arab nationalism.

06-24.title: Siam's absolute monarchy ends
06-24.body: A group of military officers and civilians staged a bloodless coup in Bangkok, forcing King Prajadhipok to accept a constitution. It ended absolute monarchy in Siam, now Thailand.

06-25.title: Our World, the first global TV broadcast
06-25.body: Our World used satellites to link broadcasters around the world in the first live international television programme, watched by hundreds of millions. The Beatles closed the British segment with the debut of "All You Need Is Love".

06-26.title: The United Nations Charter is signed
06-26.body: Delegates of 50 nations signed the Charter of the United Nations in San Francisco. The new organisation aimed to maintain international peace and security after the Second World War.

06-27.title: The Boshin War ends in Japan
06-27.body: Enomoto Takeaki surrendered at Hakodate, ending the short-lived Republic of Ezo and the Boshin War. Victory for the imperial forces cleared the way for the Meiji government to modernise Japan.

06-28.title: The Stonewall riots begin
06-28.body: A police raid on the Stonewall Inn, a gay bar in New York City, sparked days of protests. The uprising became a catalyst for the modern gay rights movement and is commemorated by Pride marches every June.

06-29.title: Space Shuttle Atlantis docks with Mir
06-29.body: Space Shuttle Atlantis docked with the Russian space station Mir, the first US–Russian docking in space in 20 years. The joint missions paved the way for the International Space Station.

06-30.title: The Congo gains independence
06-30.body: The Belgian Congo became independent as the Republic of the Congo, with Patrice Lumumba as prime minister. Within days the country slid into the Congo Crisis, a turbulent period that ended with Mobutu's dictatorship.

07-01.title: Sony launches the Walkman
07-01.body: Sony released the Walkman in Japan, a pocket-sized cassette player with lightweight headphones. It made music personal and portable, changing how people listened and paving the way for the iPod and smartphones.

07-02.title: The Civil Rights Act becomes law
07-02.body: President Lyndon B. Johnson signed the Civil Rights Act, banning discrimination based on race, colour, religion, sex or national origin and ending legal segregation in public places. It was the most sweeping civil rights law since Reconstruction.

07-03.title: The Battle of Gettysburg ends
07-03.body: After three days of fighting in Pennsylvania, Robert E. Lee's Confederate army was defeated in a failed frontal assault known as Pickett's Charge. Gettysburg ended Lee's invasion of the North and is seen as the turning point of the American Civil War.

07-04.title: Chinese astronomers record a 'guest star'
07-04.body: Song dynasty astronomers recorded a new star near Zeta Tauri, bright enough to be seen in daylight for 23 days. The supernova left behind the Crab Nebula, one of the most studied objects in astronomy.

07-05.title: France captures Algiers
07-05.body: After a three-week campaign, Hussein Dey surrendered Algiers to a French invasion force. The conquest began 132 years of French colonial rule in Algeria, which ended only with independence in 1962.

07-06.title: Napoleon wins at Wagram
07-06.body: Napoleon defeated the Austrian army of Archduke Charles at Wagram near Vienna, one of the largest battles in history up to that time. The victory forced Austria to sue for peace, ending the War of the Fifth Coalition.

07-07.title: The United States annexes Hawaii
07-07.body: President William McKinley signed the Newlands Resolution annexing the Republic of Hawaii, five years after the overthrow of Queen Liliʻuokalani. Hawaii became a US territory and, in 1959, the 50th state.

07-08.title: The Roswell incident
07-08.body: An Army Air Forces base in New Mexico announced it had recovered a "flying disc", then said it was a weather balloon. The debris came from a secret balloon project, but Roswell became the most famous UFO story in the world.

07-09.title: The Russell–Einstein Manifesto
07-09.body: Bertrand Russell released a manifesto signed by Albert Einstein and nine other leading scientists warning of the dangers of nuclear war. It led to the Pugwash Conferences, which later won the Nobel Peace Prize.

07-10.title: The Isshi incident in Japan
07-10.body: Prince Naka no Ōe and Nakatomi no Kamatari assassinated the powerful courtier Soga no Iruka at the imperial palace. The coup broke the Soga clan's dominance and led to the Taika Reforms that centralised the Japanese state.

07-11.title: Zheng He's treasure fleet sets sail
07-11.body: The Chinese admiral Zheng He sailed on the first of seven great voyages of the Ming treasure fleet. His enormous ships reached Southeast Asia, India, Arabia and East Africa, decades before Europe's age of exploration.

07-12.title: The Rolling Stones play their first gig
07-12.body: The Rolling Stones performed their first concert at the Marquee Club in London. Rooted in American blues, the band became one of the most popular and longest-lasting acts in rock music.

07-13.title: The first FIFA World Cup kicks off
07-13.body: The first football World Cup opened in Uruguay, the reigning Olympic champions, with 13 teams taking part. Uruguay beat Argentina in the final, launching what became the most watched sporting event in the world.

07-14.title: The storming of the Bastille
07-14.body: A Paris crowd seeking gunpowder stormed the Bastille, a royal fortress and prison that symbolised royal tyranny. Its fall became the emblem of the French Revolution, and 14 July is France's national day.

07-15.title: Psy releases Gangnam Style
07-15.body: South Korean singer Psy released "Gangnam Style". Its music video became the first on YouTube to pass one billion views, and it carried the Korean Wave of pop culture to a global audience.

07-16.title: Comet Shoemaker–Levy 9 hits Jupiter
07-16.body: The first of more than 20 fragments of Comet Shoemaker–Levy 9 struck Jupiter, leaving dark scars larger than the Earth. It was the first collision between two Solar System bodies ever directly observed.

07-17.title: The Spanish Civil War begins
07-17.body: Nationalist army officers launched a coup against the Second Spanish Republic, starting in Spanish Morocco. Its partial failure led to three years of civil war and Francisco Franco's dictatorship.

07-18.title: Pedro II is crowned Emperor of Brazil
07-18.body: Fifteen-year-old Pedro II was crowned in Rio de Janeiro. His reign of nearly half a century brought stability, economic growth and the abolition of slavery, before the monarchy fell in 1889.

07-19.title: The Seneca Falls Convention opens
07-19.body: The first women's rights convention in the United States opened in Seneca Falls, New York. Its Declaration of Sentiments, which demanded equal rights including the vote, launched the American women's suffrage movement.

07-20.title: Apollo 11 lands on the Moon
07-20.body: The lunar module Eagle landed on the Sea of Tranquillity, and Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin became the first people to walk on the Moon. Watched by some 600 million people, it fulfilled President Kennedy's goal for the decade.

07-21.title: The world's first woman prime minister
07-21.body: Sirimavo Bandaranaike was sworn in as prime minister of Ceylon, now Sri Lanka, after leading her party to election victory. She became the world's first elected female head of government.

07-22.title: Gia Long unifies Vietnam
07-22.body: Nguyễn Phúc Ánh captured Hanoi, completing the unification of Vietnam after decades of civil war. Ruling as Emperor Gia Long, he founded the Nguyễn dynasty, the country's last.

07-23.title: The Chinese Communist Party holds its first congress
07-23.body: A dozen delegates met secretly in a house in Shanghai's French Concession for the first congress of the Chinese Communist Party. Mao Zedong was among them; 28 years later the party ruled China.

07-24.title: The Treaty of Lausanne is signed
07-24.body: The Treaty of Lausanne ended the conflict between Turkey and the Allies after the First World War. It recognised the borders of the new Republic of Turkey and replaced the punitive Treaty of Sèvres.

07-25.title: India's first woman president
07-25.body: Pratibha Patil was sworn in as the 12th President of India, the first woman to hold the office. A lawyer and veteran politician from Maharashtra, she served a full five-year term.

07-26.title: Zamenhof launches Esperanto
07-26.body: Ludwik Zamenhof published the first book describing Esperanto, a language he designed to be easy to learn and to foster understanding between peoples. It became the most widely spoken constructed language in the world.

07-27.title: The Korean War armistice is signed
07-27.body: An armistice ended the fighting of the Korean War and created a demilitarised zone near the 38th parallel. No peace treaty was ever signed, and the peninsula remains divided.

07-28.title: San Martín declares Peru independent
07-28.body: In Lima, General José de San Martín proclaimed the independence of Peru from Spain. Fighting continued until 1824, but 28 July is celebrated as Peru's national day.

07-29.title: The Fellowship of the Ring is published
07-29.body: J. R. R. Tolkien's The Fellowship of the Ring, the first volume of The Lord of the Rings, was published in London. The trilogy became one of the best-selling novels ever and shaped modern fantasy fiction.

07-30.title: England wins the World Cup
07-30.body: England beat West Germany 4–2 after extra time at Wembley Stadium, with Geoff Hurst scoring a hat-trick. It remains England's only men's World Cup victory.

07-31.title: First ascent of K2
07-31.body: Italian climbers Lino Lacedelli and Achille Compagnoni reached the summit of K2 on the border of Pakistan and China. The world's second-highest mountain is considered far harder and more dangerous to climb than Everest.

08-01.title: Nelson wins the Battle of the Nile
08-01.body: A British fleet under Horatio Nelson attacked the French fleet anchored in Aboukir Bay, Egypt, destroying or capturing most of it. The victory stranded Napoleon's army in Egypt and restored British naval dominance in the Mediterranean.

08-02.title: Einstein's letter warns of the atomic bomb
08-02.body: Physicist Leo Szilard drafted a letter, signed by Albert Einstein, warning President Franklin D. Roosevelt that Germany might build an atomic bomb. It prompted the first US research effort, which grew into the Manhattan Project.

08-03.title: Auckland's Sky Tower opens
08-03.body: The 328-metre Sky Tower opened in Auckland, New Zealand, as the tallest free-standing structure in the Southern Hemisphere. It quickly became the city's best-known landmark and a symbol of modern New Zealand.

08-04.title: Britain enters the First World War
08-04.body: After Germany invaded neutral Belgium, Britain declared war on Germany, bringing the British Empire into the First World War. Over the next four years the war cost millions of lives and redrew the map of Europe.

08-05.title: Bertha Benz makes the first long car journey
08-05.body: Bertha Benz drove her husband Carl's Motorwagen about 106 km from Mannheim to Pforzheim with her two sons, without telling him. The first long-distance automobile trip proved the car's practicality and generated worldwide publicity.

08-06.title: The atomic bombing of Hiroshima
08-06.body: A US bomber dropped an atomic bomb on Hiroshima, Japan, the first use of a nuclear weapon in war. Together with the bombing of Nagasaki three days later, it led to Japan's surrender and opened the nuclear age.

08-07.title: Lynne Cox swims the Bering Strait
08-07.body: American swimmer Lynne Cox swam from Little Diomede in the United States to Big Diomede in the Soviet Union through water of about 4°C. Her Cold War crossing was praised by both Reagan and Gorbachev as a gesture of goodwill.

08-08.title: Afghanistan wins full independence
08-08.body: The Treaty of Rawalpindi ended the Third Anglo-Afghan War, with Britain recognising Afghanistan's right to conduct its own foreign affairs. Afghanistan celebrates its independence day every August.

08-09.title: The women's march on Pretoria
08-09.body: About 20,000 women of all races marched to the Union Buildings in Pretoria to protest against apartheid pass laws being extended to women. The date is now celebrated as National Women's Day in South Africa.

08-10.title: The Louvre opens as a public museum
08-10.body: During the French Revolution, the former royal palace of the Louvre opened as a public museum displaying 537 paintings. It is now the most visited museum in the world.

08-11.title: Francis Light founds George Town
08-11.body: Francis Light of the British East India Company took possession of Penang Island and founded George Town. It became the first British settlement in Southeast Asia and a thriving multicultural port, now a World Heritage Site.

08-12.title: Sue the T. rex is discovered
08-12.body: Fossil hunter Sue Hendrickson found the skeleton of a Tyrannosaurus rex near Faith, South Dakota. Named Sue in her honour, it is one of the largest and most complete T. rex specimens ever found.

08-13.title: Britain captures Havana
08-13.body: After a two-month siege during the Seven Years' War, the Spanish surrendered Havana to British forces. Britain returned the city a year later in exchange for Florida, but the occupation opened Cuba to wider trade.

08-14.title: The Atlantic Charter is issued
08-14.body: After meeting secretly aboard warships off Newfoundland, Winston Churchill and Franklin D. Roosevelt issued the Atlantic Charter, setting out shared goals for the post-war world. Its principles inspired the United Nations.

08-15.title: India becomes independent
08-15.body: At midnight, India gained independence from British rule, and Jawaharlal Nehru became its first prime minister. Independence came with the partition of British India into India and Pakistan.

08-16.title: Manila's all-steel church is consecrated
08-16.body: San Sebastian Church in Manila was consecrated. Built from prefabricated steel parts shipped from Belgium, it is the only all-steel church in Asia and a national historical landmark of the Philippines.

08-17.title: Indonesia declares independence
08-17.body: Sukarno and Mohammad Hatta proclaimed Indonesia's independence in Jakarta, two days after Japan's surrender. The Dutch resisted, and only after four years of revolution did the Netherlands recognise the new nation.

08-18.title: US women win the right to vote
08-18.body: Tennessee became the 36th state to ratify the 19th Amendment, providing the majority needed to add it to the US Constitution. It barred denial of the vote on the basis of sex, the culmination of decades of suffrage campaigning.

08-19.title: London's first electric taxis
08-19.body: The Bersey Electric Cab entered service in London, the city's first motorised taxi. The battery-powered cabs were withdrawn after two years, but they foreshadowed the electric vehicles of today.

08-20.title: The NFL is founded in Canton, Ohio
08-20.body: Representatives of professional American football teams met at a car showroom in Canton, Ohio, to form the American Professional Football Conference. Renamed the National Football League in 1922, it became the most lucrative sports league in the world.

08-21.title: The Mona Lisa is stolen
08-21.body: Vincenzo Peruggia, a former Louvre worker, stole Leonardo da Vinci's Mona Lisa by hiding in the museum overnight. The painting was recovered in Florence two years later, and the theft made it the most famous painting in the world.

08-22.title: Madras is founded
08-22.body: Officials of the East India Company obtained a strip of coastal land from local rulers of the Vijayanagara Empire. There they built Fort St. George, around which grew the city of Madras, now Chennai.

08-23.title: The Baltic Way human chain
08-23.body: About two million people joined hands in a chain over 675 km long across Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania. The peaceful protest against Soviet rule marked 50 years since the Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact and helped the Baltic states regain independence.

08-24.title: Pluto is reclassified as a dwarf planet
08-24.body: The International Astronomical Union adopted a formal definition of a planet, reclassifying Pluto as a dwarf planet. The Solar System officially went from nine planets to eight.

08-25.title: Voyager 1 reaches interstellar space
08-25.body: NASA's Voyager 1, launched in 1977, crossed the heliopause into interstellar space, the first human-made object to do so. It still carries the Golden Record of sounds and images from Earth.

08-26.title: Satyajit Ray's Pather Panchali premieres
08-26.body: Pather Panchali, Satyajit Ray's first film, was released in Calcutta. Its realist portrait of a poor Bengali family won international acclaim and brought Indian art cinema to a world audience.

08-27.title: The shortest war in history
08-27.body: After a usurper seized the throne of Zanzibar, British warships bombarded the palace. The sultanate surrendered in less than an hour, making the Anglo-Zanzibar War the shortest recorded war in history.

08-28.title: Martin Luther King's 'I Have a Dream'
08-28.body: Speaking at the Lincoln Memorial to some 250,000 people at the March on Washington, Martin Luther King Jr. called for an end to racism. The speech became one of the most famous in American history.

08-29.title: Treaty of Nanking ends the First Opium War
08-29.body: China signed the Treaty of Nanking with Britain, ceding Hong Kong Island, opening five ports to foreign trade and paying an indemnity. It was the first of the "unequal treaties" that China came to see as a century of humiliation.

08-30.title: The Philippine Revolution's first battle
08-30.body: Katipunan revolutionaries led by Andrés Bonifacio attacked a Spanish powder magazine at San Juan del Monte near Manila. The attack failed, but it marked the start of armed revolt against more than three centuries of Spanish rule.

08-31.title: Sultan Murad V is deposed
08-31.body: Ottoman Sultan Murad V was deposed after only 93 days on the throne on grounds of mental illness. His brother Abdul Hamid II succeeded him and ruled the empire autocratically for 33 years.

09-01.title: Sikh scripture installed at the Golden Temple
09-01.body: Guru Arjan installed the Adi Granth, the compiled scripture of Sikhism, in the Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple) in Amritsar. Later expanded as the Guru Granth Sahib, it is revered by Sikhs as their eternal living Guru.

09-02.title: Japan formally surrenders
09-02.body: Aboard the USS Missouri in Tokyo Bay, Japanese representatives signed the Instrument of Surrender before the Allied powers. The ceremony formally ended the Second World War, six years and a day after it began.

09-03.title: Australia's flag flies for the first time
09-03.body: The winning designs of a national flag competition were announced, and a large version flew over the Royal Exhibition Building in Melbourne. The Southern Cross and Commonwealth Star design became Australia's national flag; 3 September is Flag Day.

09-04.title: The last Western Roman emperor is deposed
09-04.body: The Germanic general Odoacer deposed the boy emperor Romulus Augustulus at Ravenna and declined to name a successor. Historians traditionally date the fall of the Western Roman Empire to this event.

09-05.title: Treaty of Portsmouth ends the Russo-Japanese War
09-05.body: Russia and Japan signed a peace treaty at Portsmouth, New Hampshire, mediated by President Theodore Roosevelt. Japan's victory, the first of an Asian power over a European one in modern times, made it a world power, and Roosevelt won the Nobel Peace Prize.

09-06.title: Argentina's first military coup
09-06.body: General José Félix Uriburu overthrew the elected president Hipólito Yrigoyen. It was the first of six military coups in 20th-century Argentina, opening a long period of political instability known as the Infamous Decade.

09-07.title: Brazil declares independence
09-07.body: On the banks of the Ipiranga stream near São Paulo, Prince Pedro declared Brazil independent from Portugal with the cry "Independence or death!". He became Emperor Pedro I of the new Empire of Brazil.

09-08.title: SEATO is founded in Manila
09-08.body: Eight nations signed the Manila Pact, creating the Southeast Asia Treaty Organization to contain communism in the region. Modelled on NATO, it lacked a unified command and was dissolved in 1977.

09-09.title: Barnard discovers Jupiter's moon Amalthea
09-09.body: Using the great refractor at Lick Observatory in California, Edward Emerson Barnard discovered Amalthea, a small inner moon of Jupiter. It was the first new Jovian moon since Galileo, and the last moon found by eye rather than photography.

09-10.title: Portugal recognises Guinea-Bissau
09-10.body: Portugal formally recognised the independence of Guinea-Bissau, which had declared itself independent a year earlier after a long guerrilla war led by Amílcar Cabral's movement. It was the first of Portugal's African colonies to become free.

09-11.title: Vivekananda addresses the World's Parliament of Religions
09-11.body: On the opening day of the first Parliament of the World's Religions in Chicago, Swami Vivekananda began his address "Sisters and brothers of America". His speeches introduced Hinduism and yoga philosophy to a wide Western audience.

09-12.title: Yax Nuun Ahiin I becomes ruler of Tikal
09-12.body: Yax Nuun Ahiin I took the throne of the Maya city of Tikal, in today's Guatemala, as recorded in carved inscriptions. His reign reflected the influence of the distant metropolis of Teotihuacan over the Maya lowlands.

09-13.title: Super Mario Bros. is released
09-13.body: Nintendo released Super Mario Bros. in Japan for the Famicom. Designed by Shigeru Miyamoto, it defined the side-scrolling platform game, helped revive the video game industry and made Mario a global icon.

09-14.title: Gravitational waves detected for the first time
09-14.body: The twin LIGO detectors in the United States recorded gravitational waves from two black holes merging over a billion light years away. The detection confirmed a key prediction of Einstein's general relativity and earned a Nobel Prize in 2017.

09-15.title: Central America declares independence
09-15.body: Leaders meeting in Guatemala City signed the Act of Independence of Central America, ending Spanish rule. Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras and Nicaragua all celebrate the date as their independence day.

09-16.title: Malaysia is formed
09-16.body: Malaya united with Singapore, North Borneo (Sabah) and Sarawak to form Malaysia. Singapore left the federation two years later to become an independent state.

09-17.title: Solidarity is founded in Poland
09-17.body: Delegates from across Poland founded Solidarity, led by shipyard electrician Lech Wałęsa, the first independent trade union in the Soviet bloc. At its peak it had ten million members and helped bring down communism in 1989.

09-18.title: Nerva becomes Roman emperor
09-18.body: After the assassination of Domitian, the Senate proclaimed the elderly Nerva emperor. He was the first of the "Five Good Emperors", whose adoption of capable heirs gave Rome nearly a century of stability.

09-19.title: New Zealand women win the vote
09-19.body: The Electoral Act 1893 became law, making New Zealand the first self-governing country to give all women the right to vote in national elections. The campaign was led by Kate Sheppard, who appears on the country's ten-dollar note.

09-20.title: Italian troops capture Rome
09-20.body: Italian troops entered Rome through a breach near the Porta Pia, ending the Pope's temporal rule over the city. Rome became the capital of a unified Italy the following year.

09-21.title: Tolkien's The Hobbit is published
09-21.body: J. R. R. Tolkien's children's novel The Hobbit was published in London. Its success led his publisher to ask for a sequel, which grew into The Lord of the Rings.

09-22.title: The Vela incident
09-22.body: A US Vela satellite detected a double flash of light over the southern Indian Ocean near the Prince Edward Islands. It is widely believed to have been an undeclared nuclear test, though its origin has never been officially confirmed.

09-23.title: Wellesley wins the Battle of Assaye
09-23.body: Major General Arthur Wellesley, the future Duke of Wellington, defeated a much larger Maratha army at Assaye in western India. He later called it the finest thing he ever did in the field, and it helped Britain dominate India.

09-24.title: Cambodia restores its monarchy
09-24.body: After years of civil war and the Khmer Rouge genocide, a new constitution restored the Cambodian monarchy and Norodom Sihanouk became king again. He had first taken the throne in 1941.

09-25.title: The birth of Peking opera
09-25.body: The Four Great Anhui Troupes arrived in Beijing to perform for the Qianlong Emperor's 80th birthday. Blending their style with other regional forms, they gave rise to Peking opera, now recognised by UNESCO as world heritage.

09-26.title: Stanislav Petrov averts nuclear war
09-26.body: Soviet officer Stanislav Petrov judged that an early-warning alert of incoming US missiles was a false alarm and did not report it as an attack. His decision may have prevented a nuclear war; the alarm was caused by sunlight on clouds.

09-27.title: Champollion deciphers hieroglyphs
09-27.body: Jean-François Champollion read his letter to the Académie des Inscriptions in Paris announcing how he had deciphered Egyptian hieroglyphs, using the Rosetta Stone. It opened ancient Egyptian civilisation to modern study.

09-28.title: Fleming discovers penicillin
09-28.body: Returning from holiday to his London laboratory, Alexander Fleming noticed a mould that had killed bacteria in a culture dish. Penicillin, mass-produced from the 1940s, became the first widely used antibiotic and has saved millions of lives.

09-29.title: The British Mandate for Palestine takes effect
09-29.body: The League of Nations mandate for Palestine came into force, placing Palestine and Transjordan under British administration. It incorporated the Balfour Declaration's promise of a Jewish national home, shaping the region's conflicts.

09-30.title: The Munich Agreement is signed
09-30.body: Germany, Britain, France and Italy agreed that Czechoslovakia must hand the Sudetenland to Nazi Germany, without Czechoslovakia being consulted. Chamberlain claimed "peace for our time", but Hitler occupied the rest of the country months later.

10-01.title: Mao proclaims the People's Republic of China
10-01.body: From the Gate of Heavenly Peace overlooking Tiananmen Square, Mao Zedong proclaimed the founding of the People's Republic of China. Victory in the civil war ended decades of upheaval and drove the Nationalist government to Taiwan.

10-02.title: Thurgood Marshall joins the Supreme Court
10-02.body: Thurgood Marshall was sworn in as the first African-American justice of the US Supreme Court. As a lawyer he had won Brown v. Board of Education, and he served on the court for 24 years.

10-03.title: Nadine Gordimer wins the Nobel Prize
10-03.body: South African novelist Nadine Gordimer was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature, the first South African to receive it. Her novels exposed the moral and human costs of apartheid, and several were banned at home.

10-04.title: Carving begins on Mount Rushmore
10-04.body: Sculptor Gutzon Borglum and about 400 workers began carving Mount Rushmore in South Dakota. The 18-metre faces of four presidents took 14 years to complete, on land sacred to the Lakota Sioux.

10-05.title: The Women's March on Versailles
10-05.body: Thousands of Parisian women, angry at the price and scarcity of bread, marched to the royal palace at Versailles. They forced King Louis XVI and his family to move to Paris, a turning point of the French Revolution.

10-06.title: The Yom Kippur War begins
10-06.body: On the Jewish holy day of Yom Kippur, Egypt and Syria launched a surprise attack on Israeli positions in Sinai and the Golan Heights. The war led to an Arab oil embargo and, eventually, the Egypt–Israel peace treaty of 1979.

10-07.title: The first predicted asteroid impact
10-07.body: The small asteroid 2008 TC3 exploded over the Nubian Desert in Sudan, less than a day after it was discovered. It was the first asteroid impact predicted in advance, and students later recovered hundreds of its meteorites.

10-08.title: The Council of Chalcedon opens
10-08.body: Hundreds of bishops gathered at Chalcedon, across the Bosporus from Constantinople, for the fourth ecumenical council. Its definition of Christ as one person in two natures split the Eastern churches and still divides Christians today.

10-09.title: The Universal Postal Union is founded
10-09.body: Delegates of 22 countries signed the Treaty of Bern, creating the General Postal Union, soon renamed the Universal Postal Union. It set uniform rates for international letters, and 9 October is World Post Day.

10-10.title: The Wuchang Uprising
10-10.body: Revolutionary soldiers rose up in Wuchang, central China, sparking the Xinhai Revolution. Within months the Qing dynasty collapsed, ending more than two thousand years of imperial rule; the date is celebrated in Taiwan as National Day.

10-11.title: The University of Sydney is inaugurated
10-11.body: The University of Sydney, Australia's first university, was formally inaugurated with 24 students. It opened university education to the colony, though women were not admitted until 1881.

10-12.title: The iron lung is first used
10-12.body: At Boston Children's Hospital, a girl paralysed by polio was placed in the first iron lung, a negative-pressure ventilator that breathed for her. Iron lungs saved thousands of lives during the polio epidemics before vaccines arrived.

10-13.title: The Treaty of Kars fixes Turkey's eastern border
10-13.body: Turkey's Grand National Assembly and the Soviet republics of Armenia, Azerbaijan and Georgia signed the Treaty of Kars. It established the border between Turkey and the South Caucasus that still exists today.

10-14.title: Ambedkar converts to Buddhism
10-14.body: B. R. Ambedkar, architect of India's constitution and champion of the Dalits, converted to Buddhism in Nagpur along with hundreds of thousands of followers. The mass conversion rejected caste discrimination and revived Buddhism in India.

10-15.title: Air India makes its first flight
10-15.body: J. R. D. Tata flew the first flight of Tata Air Lines, carrying mail from Karachi to Bombay. The airline was renamed Air India in 1946 and became the country's national carrier.

10-16.title: Walt and Roy Disney found their studio
10-16.body: Brothers Walt and Roy Disney founded the Disney Brothers Cartoon Studio in Hollywood. Home of Mickey Mouse and the first feature-length animated film, it grew into one of the world's largest entertainment companies.

10-17.title: Kepler observes a new star
10-17.body: Johannes Kepler began observing a brilliant new star in the constellation Ophiuchus. Kepler's Supernova was the last supernova seen in our own galaxy with the naked eye, and it challenged the belief that the heavens never change.

10-18.title: Venera 4 probes the atmosphere of Venus
10-18.body: The Soviet probe Venera 4 descended through the atmosphere of Venus, sending back the first direct measurements from another planet's atmosphere. It revealed that Venus is far hotter and denser than scientists had expected.

10-19.title: British surrender at Yorktown
10-19.body: General Cornwallis surrendered his army to American and French forces after the siege of Yorktown, Virginia. It was the last major battle of the American Revolutionary War and led Britain to negotiate peace.

10-20.title: Maria Theresa inherits the Habsburg lands
10-20.body: On the death of her father Charles VI, Maria Theresa succeeded to the Habsburg lands under the Pragmatic Sanction. She defended her inheritance in the War of the Austrian Succession and ruled for 40 years as a reforming monarch.

10-21.title: The US–North Korea Agreed Framework
10-21.body: North Korea agreed to freeze its plutonium programme in return for fuel oil and two light-water nuclear reactors. The deal held for eight years before collapsing, and North Korea later tested nuclear weapons.

10-22.title: Nixon in China premieres in Houston
10-22.body: John Adams's opera Nixon in China, about President Nixon's 1972 visit to Mao Zedong, premiered at the Houston Grand Opera. It became one of the most performed American operas of its time.

10-23.title: The Hungarian Revolution begins
10-23.body: A student demonstration in Budapest grew into a nationwide revolt against the Soviet-backed government. Soviet tanks crushed the uprising within three weeks, and some 200,000 Hungarians fled abroad.

10-24.title: Henry Parkes calls for Australian federation
10-24.body: In a speech at Tenterfield, New South Wales premier Henry Parkes called for the six Australian colonies to unite under one federal government. The colonies federated as the Commonwealth of Australia in 1901, and Parkes is called the father of federation.
