10-25.title: Dirk Hartog leaves his plate in Australia
10-25.body: Dutch captain Dirk Hartog landed on an island in Shark Bay, Western Australia, and nailed an inscribed pewter plate to a post. It is the oldest known artefact of European exploration in Australia.

10-26.title: Admiral Yi wins at Myeongnyang
10-26.body: With just 13 ships, Korean admiral Yi Sun-sin defeated a Japanese fleet of over 130 in the narrow, fast-flowing Myeongnyang Strait. The victory helped stop the Japanese invasion of Korea and made Yi a national hero.

10-27.title: The New York City Subway opens
10-27.body: The first underground line of the New York City Subway opened, running from City Hall to Harlem. It grew into one of the largest rapid transit systems in the world, running around the clock.

10-28.title: Indonesia Raya is first performed
10-28.body: At the Second Youth Congress in Batavia, composer Wage Rudolf Supratman played "Indonesia Raya" on his violin. The same congress adopted the Youth Pledge of one nation and one language, and the song became Indonesia's national anthem.

10-29.title: Galileo visits the asteroid Gaspra
10-29.body: On its way to Jupiter, NASA's Galileo spacecraft flew past the asteroid 951 Gaspra, taking the first close-up images of an asteroid. It revealed a cratered, irregular rock about 18 kilometres long.

10-30.title: The War of the Worlds broadcast
10-30.body: Orson Welles's radio adaptation of H. G. Wells's The War of the Worlds, presented as a series of news bulletins, aired on CBS. Newspapers reported panic among listeners, and the broadcast became a famous lesson in the power of media.

10-31.title: Luther's Ninety-five Theses
10-31.body: Martin Luther sent his Ninety-five Theses criticising the sale of indulgences to the Archbishop of Mainz, and by tradition posted them on a church door in Wittenberg. The act sparked the Protestant Reformation.

11-01.title: India redraws its states by language
11-01.body: Under the States Reorganisation Act, India's internal borders were redrawn largely along linguistic lines, creating states such as Kerala, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh. It reshaped Indian federalism and the political map of the country.

11-02.title: Australia's 'Emu War' begins
11-02.body: Soldiers armed with machine guns were sent to Western Australia to cull thousands of emus damaging farmers' wheat crops. The birds proved remarkably elusive, and the much-mocked operation was soon called off.

11-03.title: The Fashoda Incident ends
11-03.body: France ordered its troops to withdraw from Fashoda on the Upper Nile, ending a tense standoff with Britain over control of Sudan. The settlement ended the race for Africa between the two powers and paved the way for their Entente Cordiale.

11-04.title: Tutankhamun's tomb is found
11-04.body: Howard Carter's team in Egypt's Valley of the Kings uncovered the first step leading down to the tomb of the pharaoh Tutankhamun. Almost intact, with treasures including a solid gold coffin and mask, it is the most famous archaeological find ever made.

11-05.title: India launches its Mars mission
11-05.body: The Indian Space Research Organisation launched the Mars Orbiter Mission, or Mangalyaan. When it reached Mars in 2014, India became the first nation to succeed at its first attempt and the first Asian country to orbit the planet.

11-06.title: George Eliot submits her first story
11-06.body: Mary Ann Evans sent the first of her Scenes of Clerical Life to the publisher John Blackwood, launching her career as a novelist. Writing as George Eliot, she went on to write Middlemarch, one of the greatest English novels.

11-07.title: Singapore's MRT opens
11-07.body: Singapore's first Mass Rapid Transit line opened between Yio Chu Kang and Toa Payoh. The network became the backbone of transport in the city-state and a model of urban rail planning.

11-08.title: The first Qing emperor enthroned in Beijing
11-08.body: The young Shunzhi Emperor was enthroned in Beijing after the fall of the Ming dynasty, becoming the first emperor of the Manchu Qing dynasty to rule China. The Qing governed China until 1912.

11-09.title: The Berlin Wall falls
11-09.body: After an East German spokesman mistakenly announced that the borders were open with immediate effect, crowds surged through the checkpoints of the Berlin Wall. Its fall led to German reunification and symbolised the end of the Cold War.

11-10.title: Stanley finds Livingstone
11-10.body: Journalist Henry Morton Stanley found the missing missionary-explorer David Livingstone at Ujiji, near Lake Tanganyika. His reported greeting, "Dr. Livingstone, I presume?", became one of the most famous lines in exploration.

11-11.title: The First World War armistice
11-11.body: Germany and the Allies signed an armistice in a railway carriage in the Forest of Compiègne, and fighting stopped at 11 a.m. The date is observed as Armistice Day or Remembrance Day in many countries.

11-12.title: Philae lands on a comet
11-12.body: The European Space Agency's Philae lander, carried by the Rosetta spacecraft, touched down on comet 67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko, the first landing on a comet. It bounced twice but still sent back data about the comet's surface.

11-13.title: Zaian victory at El Herri
11-13.body: Zaian Berber fighters inflicted a heavy defeat on a French column at El Herri in Morocco's Middle Atlas. It was one of France's worst defeats in its colonial wars in North Africa and prolonged the Zaian War for years.

11-14.title: Astronomers discover Sedna
11-14.body: Astronomers at Palomar Observatory discovered Sedna, a distant body with an extraordinarily elongated orbit that takes over 11,000 years to circle the Sun. Its discovery helped spur the debate that redefined what counts as a planet.

11-15.title: Brazil becomes a republic
11-15.body: A military coup led by Marshal Deodoro da Fonseca overthrew Emperor Pedro II and proclaimed Brazil a republic. The imperial family went into exile, ending the only long-lasting monarchy in the Americas.

11-16.title: The First Salute to the American flag
11-16.body: The Dutch fort on the Caribbean island of Sint Eustatius returned the salute of the American warship Andrew Doria. It was the first time a foreign power saluted the flag of the newly independent United States.

11-17.title: The 15-year-old Dalai Lama takes power
11-17.body: As Chinese forces advanced into Tibet, the 14th Dalai Lama, aged 15, was enthroned with full political authority. Nine years later he fled into exile in India.

11-18.title: Minecraft is officially released
11-18.body: Swedish studio Mojang released the full version of Minecraft after years of public testing. Its open-ended world of blocks to mine and build with made it the best-selling video game of all time.

11-19.title: Pelé scores his thousandth goal
11-19.body: Brazilian forward Pelé scored his 1,000th goal, from a penalty for Santos against Vasco da Gama at the Maracanã stadium in Rio de Janeiro. Widely regarded as the greatest footballer ever, he won three World Cups with Brazil.

11-20.title: The Nuremberg trials begin
11-20.body: An international military tribunal opened in Nuremberg to try leading Nazis for war crimes, crimes against peace and crimes against humanity. The trials established that individuals can be held responsible under international law.

11-21.title: Edison announces the phonograph
11-21.body: Thomas Edison announced his invention of the phonograph, the first device able both to record sound and to play it back. It founded the recorded music industry.

11-22.title: Lebanon becomes independent
11-22.body: After protests forced France to release Lebanon's arrested president and ministers, France accepted the end of its mandate. The date is celebrated as Lebanon's Independence Day.

11-23.title: Hubble shows Andromeda is another galaxy
11-23.body: The New York Times reported Edwin Hubble's discovery that the Andromeda Nebula lies far beyond the Milky Way. His measurements proved that our galaxy is one of countless others in the universe.

11-24.title: Darwin publishes On the Origin of Species
11-24.body: Charles Darwin's On the Origin of Species, setting out the theory of evolution by natural selection, was published in London and sold out on its first day. It became the foundation of modern biology.

11-25.title: Suriname becomes independent
11-25.body: The South American country of Suriname gained independence from the Netherlands, with Johan Ferrier as its first president. Many Surinamese emigrated to the Netherlands around the time of independence.

11-26.title: Casablanca premieres
11-26.body: The film Casablanca, starring Humphrey Bogart and Ingrid Bergman, premiered in New York, weeks after Allied troops captured the Moroccan city. It won the Oscar for Best Picture and became one of the most quoted films ever made.

11-27.title: Alfred Nobel signs his will
11-27.body: At the Swedish-Norwegian Club in Paris, Alfred Nobel, inventor of dynamite, signed a will leaving most of his fortune to fund annual prizes. The Nobel Prizes were first awarded in 1901.

11-28.title: Albania declares independence
11-28.body: During the First Balkan War, delegates meeting in Vlorë declared Albania independent of the Ottoman Empire, with Ismail Qemali as head of government. The date is Albania's national Independence Day.

11-29.title: The UN votes to partition Palestine
11-29.body: The United Nations General Assembly approved a plan to divide British Mandatory Palestine into separate Jewish and Arab states, with Jerusalem under international control. Israel declared independence months later, and the plan's legacy still shapes the conflict.

11-30.title: The Balmis vaccine expedition sets sail
11-30.body: Physician Francisco Javier de Balmis sailed from A Coruña to carry smallpox vaccine to Spain's colonies, keeping it alive by passing it between orphan boys. The expedition vaccinated hundreds of thousands in the Americas and the Philippines.

12-01.title: The Antarctic Treaty is signed
12-01.body: Twelve countries, including the United States and the Soviet Union, signed the Antarctic Treaty in Washington. It banned military activity and nuclear tests on the continent and set it aside for peaceful science, the first arms control agreement of the Cold War.

12-02.title: The first nuclear chain reaction
12-02.body: Under the stands of a sports field at the University of Chicago, Enrico Fermi's team achieved the first self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction in Chicago Pile-1. It opened the way to both nuclear power and the atomic bomb.

12-03.title: The first human heart transplant
12-03.body: At Groote Schuur Hospital in Cape Town, surgeon Christiaan Barnard transplanted the heart of a young road accident victim into Louis Washkansky, a grocer with heart disease. He lived for 18 days, and the operation made heart transplantation a reality.

12-04.title: India's governor bans sati
12-04.body: Governor-General Lord William Bentinck outlawed sati, the practice of burning a widow on her husband's funeral pyre, in the Bengal Presidency. The ban followed years of campaigning by reformer Ram Mohan Roy.

12-05.title: The Great Smog of London begins
12-05.body: Cold, windless weather trapped coal smoke over London, creating a thick smog that lasted five days and caused thousands of deaths. It led to the Clean Air Act of 1956, a landmark in environmental law.

12-06.title: The 13th Amendment abolishes US slavery
12-06.body: Georgia became the 27th state to ratify the Thirteenth Amendment, adding it to the US Constitution. The amendment abolished slavery throughout the United States, freeing the last enslaved people after the Civil War.

12-07.title: Galileo arrives at Jupiter
12-07.body: NASA's Galileo spacecraft entered orbit around Jupiter, the first probe to orbit an outer planet, and released a probe into the planet's atmosphere. Its discoveries included evidence of a salty ocean beneath the ice of the moon Europa.

12-08.title: The Belovezha Accords end the Soviet Union
12-08.body: The leaders of Russia, Ukraine and Belarus met in a hunting lodge in the Belovezha Forest and declared that the Soviet Union had ceased to exist. They founded the Commonwealth of Independent States in its place.

12-09.title: Smallpox is declared eradicated
12-09.body: A World Health Organization commission certified that smallpox had been eradicated worldwide, after a global vaccination campaign. It remains the only human infectious disease ever wiped out.

12-10.title: Democracy returns to Argentina
12-10.body: Raúl Alfonsín took office as president of Argentina, ending more than seven years of military dictatorship. His government prosecuted leaders of the junta for human rights abuses, an early example of transitional justice.

12-11.title: Apollo 17 lands on the Moon
12-11.body: Apollo 17's lunar module landed in the Taurus–Littrow valley, and Eugene Cernan and geologist Harrison Schmitt spent three days exploring. They were the last people to walk on the Moon.

12-12.title: Kenya becomes a republic
12-12.body: Exactly a year after independence from Britain, Kenya became a republic, with Jomo Kenyatta as its first president. The date is celebrated every year as Jamhuri Day.

12-13.title: Gershwin's An American in Paris premieres
12-13.body: George Gershwin's An American in Paris, a symphonic poem inspired by his stay in France and complete with taxi horns, premiered at Carnegie Hall. Its fusion of jazz and classical music made it one of his most popular works.

12-14.title: Amundsen reaches the South Pole
12-14.body: Norwegian explorer Roald Amundsen and four companions became the first people to reach the South Pole, using dog sleds and skis. They arrived five weeks ahead of Robert Falcon Scott's British team.

12-15.title: Venera 7 lands on Venus
12-15.body: The Soviet probe Venera 7 made the first soft landing on another planet, transmitting data from the surface of Venus for 23 minutes. It recorded a surface temperature of about 475°C.

12-16.title: Bangladesh wins its independence war
12-16.body: Pakistani forces in Dhaka surrendered to Indian and Bangladeshi forces, ending the Bangladesh Liberation War. The new nation of Bangladesh celebrates 16 December as Victory Day.

12-17.title: The Aztec sun stone is unearthed
12-17.body: Workers repaving the Zócalo, the main square of Mexico City, uncovered a huge carved basalt disc, the Aztec sun stone. It became one of the best-known symbols of Mexican identity and is displayed in the National Museum of Anthropology.

12-18.title: The Battle of Mbumbi in Kongo
12-18.body: Portuguese forces from Angola and their Imbangala allies defeated an army of the Kingdom of Kongo at Mbumbi. The Kongo struck back weeks later, and the war soured Kongo's relations with Portugal for decades.

12-19.title: Britain agrees to return Hong Kong to China
12-19.body: Margaret Thatcher and Zhao Ziyang signed the Sino-British Joint Declaration, under which Hong Kong would return to Chinese sovereignty in 1997. China promised to keep the territory's systems for 50 years under "one country, two systems".

12-20.title: Portugal hands Macau to China
12-20.body: Portugal transferred sovereignty over Macau to China, ending more than four centuries of Portuguese presence. It was the last European colony in Asia.

12-21.title: Snow White premieres in Los Angeles
12-21.body: Walt Disney's Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs, the first full-length cel-animated feature film, premiered in Los Angeles. Dubbed "Disney's Folly" during production, it became a huge success and launched the era of animated features.

12-22.title: Indonesia's emergency government is formed
12-22.body: After Dutch forces captured the Indonesian capital Yogyakarta and its leaders, Sjafruddin Prawiranegara set up an emergency government in Sumatra. It kept the republic alive until the leaders were freed, and the Dutch recognised Indonesian independence in 1949.

12-23.title: Yohl Ikʼnal becomes queen of Palenque
12-23.body: Yohl Ikʼnal took the throne of the Maya city of Palenque in today's Mexico. She was the first woman known to have ruled Palenque in her own right, and she reigned for more than 20 years.

12-24.title: Verdi's Aida premieres in Cairo
12-24.body: Giuseppe Verdi's opera Aida, set in ancient Egypt, premiered at the Khedivial Opera House in Cairo. Commissioned by the khedive of Egypt, it became one of the most popular operas in the world.

12-25.title: Gorbachev resigns as Soviet president
12-25.body: In a televised address, Mikhail Gorbachev resigned as President of the Soviet Union, and the Soviet flag over the Kremlin was replaced by the Russian tricolour. The superpower formally ceased to exist the next day.

12-26.title: The Curies announce radium
12-26.body: Pierre and Marie Curie told the French Academy of Sciences that they had discovered a new, strongly radioactive element, which they named radium. Their work on radioactivity earned them a Nobel Prize and transformed physics and medicine.

12-27.title: Hagia Sophia is inaugurated
12-27.body: Emperor Justinian I inaugurated the rebuilt Hagia Sophia in Constantinople, then the largest church in the world. Its enormous dome made it a masterpiece of Byzantine architecture; it later served as a mosque, a museum and a mosque again.

12-28.title: Taksin is crowned king of Siam
12-28.body: After the fall of Ayutthaya to Burmese invaders, the general Taksin drove out the occupiers and was crowned king at Thonburi. He reunited Siam, and his capital lay across the river from what became Bangkok.

12-29.title: China is nominally reunified
12-29.body: The warlord ruling Manchuria, Zhang Xueliang, pledged allegiance to the Nationalist government in Nanjing, formally ending Chiang Kai-shek's Northern Expedition. China was reunified under the Kuomintang, at least on paper.

12-30.title: The All-India Muslim League is founded
12-30.body: The All-India Muslim League was founded in Dhaka to represent the interests of Muslims in British India. Under Muhammad Ali Jinnah it later led the campaign that created Pakistan in 1947.

12-31.title: Panama takes control of the Panama Canal
12-31.body: Under the Torrijos–Carter Treaties, the United States handed full control of the Panama Canal to Panama. The canal had been run by the United States since it opened in 1914.
